look_here_first: Look low in grasses and open sandy ground. Swanflower is a tiny erect-to-sprawling perennial with very narrow grasslike leaves and a strange brown-purple curved flower arising near the stem. The showy tube is a petaloid fused calyx/perianth, not a normal petal corolla.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small perennial herb, erect to sprawling, often hidden among grasses

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers solitary in leaf axils on slender peduncles

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: petals absent; showy structure is a curved brown-purple fused petaloid calyx/perianth

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perianth tube curved upward with a single strap-like limb

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: fruit an ovoid 5-valved capsule with many flat triangular seeds

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Narrow grasslike leaves are a major local gestalt cue but should not be used alone.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: The brown-purple flower is built from a fused petaloid calyx/perianth, not a separate corolla. The curved tube and single limb are highly distinctive.

key_traits.label: Ovary
key_traits.text: Inferior; the compact gynostemium carries the anthers and styles in the flower center.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Ovoid capsule opening by five valves; many flat triangular seeds.

key_traits.label: Ecology
key_traits.text: Central and South Texas sandy/open habitats; larval host for the pipevine swallowtail.
